subject: Data Engineering
title: When Traditional Tools Break
description: A micro-lesson that makes When Traditional Tools Break usable.

hook.text: A company's PostgreSQL database took 14 hours to run a daily report. The data outgrew the tool.

buildup.text: Traditional databases scale vertically — buy a bigger server. Eventually, no server is big enough.

discovery.text: Big data tools scale horizontally — spread the work across hundreds of cheap commodity machines.

twist.text: Horizontal scaling isn't free. It introduces network overhead, coordination complexity, and new failures.

climax.text: The moment your data doesn't fit on one machine, you've entered big data territory.

punchline.text: When one machine isn't enough, you distribute.

quiz.question: How do big data tools scale differently from traditional databases?
options: Horizontally across many machines instead of one bigger machine
By compressing all data into one file
